01What is happening

Here is what happens now.

  1. Step 1

    A customer asks AI.

    The same question they used to type into a search box. Who’s the best plumber near me?

  2. Step 2

    It answers with a few names.

    Two or three businesses, in a sentence or a short list. That short list is what your customer sees.

  3. Step 3

    It points to the pages it used.

    Links under the answer. Review sites, “best of” lists, directories. Sometimes your own website, often someone else’s page about you.

Try it now

Ask ChatGPT the question your best customer would ask. Not your business name. Their question. Then look at two things. Is your name in the answer? And whose websites do the links point to?

Ask again tomorrow. The answer may change, which is why one screenshot is a glimpse and not a measurement.

02Why it matters to your business

That answer is the new front page for your business.

  • It happens before anyone reaches your website.

    If the answer names someone else, your customer can make up their mind without ever seeing you.

  • You cannot see it happen.

    There is no ranking to check and no click to trace. You can audit a ranking. You cannot audit a conversation you were never part of.

  • Your website is one voice among many.

    AI tools lean on the sites that already write about your kind of business. Your own site is one of them, and often not the main one.

Why plain search is not enough

Asked for the best hotel in Hawaii, plain Bing search returned an electronics store’s locator page in Elmira, New York.

Six of its ten runs, 3 to 9 September 2026. Bing is not an AI tool. We run it beside six AI tools as a control, and none of the six pointed to that page once.

Keyword search matches words. It does not understand questions. That gap is the reason AI answers exist, and it is why a search ranking report cannot tell you what AI says about you.

Plain answers

Is my business invisible to AI?

Nobody can answer that in one word, including us. It is three separate questions. Can AI tools read your website? Do they say your name when a customer asks about your kind of business? And when they answer, do they point people to your site or to someone else’s page?

The free check answers the first in about a minute. The other two take asking the AI tools, more than once, and writing down what comes back. That is what the $249 written check and our monthly plans do.

What is AEO?

AEO is short for answer engine optimization, the industry’s name for showing up when people ask AI tools like ChatGPT about your kind of business. You do not need the term, only the answer to one question: what do those tools say when your customers ask?

How is this different from SEO?

SEO is about where your website lands in a list of search results. An AI answer has no list to climb. It names a few businesses and links to a few pages, and that answer is what we measure.

Which AI tools do you check?

Six: ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude and Gemma. We also run plain Bing search on the same questions as a control. Bing is not an AI tool, and we never count it as one.

Do you change my website?

No. We never touch your website, your systems or your accounts. If you want changes made, your own team or anyone you hire makes them. We only measure.

Can you promise AI will name my business?

No. Nobody controls what AI tools say, and we do not sell anything meant to change it. What we promise is the measurement. We tell you what they said and when, question by question.

Who is behind NeverRanked?

Lance Roylo, in Honolulu. NeverRanked is a small research practice, not a software company. You deal with the person doing the work, and all of it can happen in writing.
